records.transcript:
Freedom of Information / Data Management Team,

Request 719/26, and my request of 20 August 2026 (deaths of William Buckler
and Mary Doreen Williams)

1. Internal review of 719/26

I understand the Force's position is that it holds no records. I ask for an
internal review of that conclusion, because the search does not appear
capable of finding what the request describes.

South Wales Constabulary officers were present at the eviction and
demolition at Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough, between 29 November
and 6 December 1988. This is not a matter of █████. It appears in
ITV Wales footage from the time, now public on ITV's archive channel, and
in contemporary newspaper photographs and reports, which I can supply. A
police presence on that scale would have generated records: a duty or
deployment record, an operational order or briefing, an occurrence or
incident log, liaison with the Under-Sheriff or bailiffs, press office
material, and possibly photographs.

For the review, please confirm in writing:

(a) Which systems, archives and paper holdings were searched, including
pre-1990s paper records of the former Penarth/Barry division and any South
Glamorgan command records.
(b) The search terms used. Records of that period may be indexed under
"Leckwith Road", "Llandough", "BP Properties", "Buckler", "Williams", "Ty
Mawr", "eviction", "breach of the peace" or the date, rather than "Great
House Farm".
(c) Whether records of that type from 1988 were destroyed under a retention
schedule, and if so which schedule and whether any disposal record survives.
(d) Whether any records were transferred to Glamorgan Archives or the South
Wales Police Heritage Centre, with the reference if known.

If records were destroyed, a record of their destruction is itself
information I am asking for. If they are held elsewhere, please tell me
where, under your duty to advise and assist.

I was present at the eviction as a child. So far as any record contains my
personal data, please also treat this as a subject access request under
Article 15 UK GDPR.

2. Request of 20 August 2026

This request was due on 18 September 2026 and I have had no response beyond
the automatic acknowledgement. Please give me its reference and the
response. If the records are not held, please say whether they were
destroyed or passed to the Coroner.

If I do not receive the internal review outcome within 20 working days, I
will complain to the Information Commissioner.

Yours faithfully,

Requester 
greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com

email.subject: Preservation and disclosure request — Church View Close / Great House Farm, Llandough — titles WA231076 / WA240304

records.transcript:
Sirs/Madam,

I write concerning the land now comprising Church View Close, Llandough,
formerly Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, including title WA231076 and former
title WA240304.

Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd is the current registered proprietor of
WA231076. Persimmon is therefore a present link in the conveyancing chain
arising from the registration of this land in BP Properties Ltd's name in
1982–83, BP's subsequent transfer to Ideal Homes in 1993, and the later
development history.

I am conducting a documented investigation into the legitimacy of that
title chain. This is not a speculative historical enquiry. The issues arise
from identified Land Registry, conveyancing, court, planning and
public-authority records, and from specific documentary gaps which remain
unresolved.

The central issue is the historic identity and ownership of the land.

The evidence presently assembled indicates two historically distinct
parcels:

• Parcel A: the farmhouse, garden, buildings, yard and associated woodland,
which the Williams family maintains was acquired out of the Bute estate
through the Daniel Thomas transaction and subsequently became the family's
freehold interest; and

• Parcel B: the eastern agricultural fields, whose subsequent passage from
Bute to Western Ground Rents and then to BP is not presently disputed by
the family.

The significance of that distinction is that later documents repeatedly use
the expression “whole farm”, although the surviving 1939 tenancy plan is
understood to show the eastern fields only. The 1938 Bute-to-Western Ground
Rents conveyance is therefore a material title-chain question: what estate
was actually capable of being conveyed by Bute in 1938, and did that
conveyance include Parcel A?

There is further evidence requiring examination of the period from 1949 to
1974, including repeated attempts to characterise Mary's occupation of the
farmhouse parcel as tenancy or permission; the loss of the family's title
papers in about 1950–52; the 1955 possession order expressed in “whole
farm” terms but enforced everywhere except the farmhouse and garden; the
separate 1962 possession proceedings concerning the farmhouse and garden;
Mary's express assertion of ownership; and the 1974 proceedings, which were
adjourned part-heard and were never finally adjudicated on the family's
historic ownership claim.

The Court of Appeal's decision in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA
Civ 2 subsequently concerned possession, limitation and the legal effect of
the October 1974 letters. The judgment records Mary's asserted ownership
and the absence of the documents she said supported it. The present
investigation therefore distinguishes carefully between what that judgment
decided concerning possession and limitation and the separate question of
whether the documentary root and extent of WGR/BP's title to Parcel A were
ever actually established.

That distinction becomes particularly important in relation to first
registration.

HM Land Registry records show BP's first-registration applications for
WA231076 and WA240304 in 1982–83. The surviving registration material also
identifies a 31 December 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP
Pension Trust as a root of title, but that conveyance is not presently
included in the 30 July 2026 schedule of documents surviving on the
relevant first-registration files. The 1975 conveyance and plan, the
1982–83 registration material, the extent of the two titles and their later
amalgamation therefore require direct reconciliation against the underlying
documentary title.

There is also an unresolved procedural issue concerning notice and
opportunity to object during the 1982–83 first-registration process. Mary
Williams remained in occupation of the farmhouse. The family evidence
recorded on the evidence index is that notification was not received until
after her death on 26 March 1983. I am obtaining the primary notice,
service, application and registration records to establish exactly what
occurred.

The matters under investigation consequently include possible registration
mistake, procedural unfairness, material non-disclosure and, depending upon
what the primary records establish, possible █████ or deliberate
concealment. There are also unresolved public-authority record questions
involving HM Land Registry, court administration and other authorities.
These are identified as evidential questions, not asserted as established
findings against Persimmon or any individual.

Persimmon's position is therefore directly relevant because its present
registered title derives from the historic chain now being examined.

Please provide a substantive response to the following:

   1.

   *Title chain:* What documentary chain does Persimmon say establishes its
   predecessor's title to the whole of WA231076, including the farmhouse,
   garden and associated land now comprising Church View Close?
   2.

   *BP / Ideal Homes due diligence:* What title, acquisition and
   due-diligence documents were supplied to and reviewed by Persimmon in
   connection with the acquisition from Ideal Homes, including deeds, plans,
   title abstracts, searches, requisitions, Land Registry correspondence and
   enquiries concerning the extent of WA231076/WA240304?
   3.

   *Earlier title documents:* Does Persimmon hold, or has it ever held,
   copies of the 1969 WGR-to-BP Pension Trust conveyance, the 1975 BP Pension
   Trust-to-BP Properties conveyance and plan, the 1982–83 first-registration
   application/bundle, or documents explaining the inclusion of the farmhouse
   parcel within the registered extent?
   4.

   *1996 correspondence:* Does Persimmon retain the correspondence from
   March 1996 with HM Land Registry concerning WA231076, identified in the
   surviving title chronology as the last dealing on the file? If so, please
   provide a copy, subject to any properly applicable exemption or privilege.
   5.

   *Parcel A:* Has Persimmon ever reviewed the underlying documentary title
   sufficiently to satisfy itself that the farmhouse/garden parcel was
   actually comprised in the title acquired by BP, rather than being brought
   within the registered extent through the later “whole farm” description?
   6.

   *Present position:* Having regard to the matters above, does Persimmon
   maintain that its title to the farmhouse/garden parcel is supported by an
   identifiable documentary root independent of the possession and limitation
   history considered in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler?

If Persimmon maintains that the documentary title to Parcel A is
established, please identify the instrument or instruments on which that
position depends and the land those instruments actually comprise.

I am seeking voluntary or pre-action disclosure of non-privileged material
where possible. If any requested document is withheld, please identify the
document or category concerned and the basis upon which it is withheld.

*Preservation notice*

Please treat this correspondence as formal notice to preserve all documents
and electronically stored information within Persimmon's possession,
custody or control that may be relevant to the title, acquisition,
registration, extent, occupation, planning or development of this land.

This includes historical material inherited from BP Properties, Ideal Homes
or any other predecessor, together with deeds, conveyances, plans, title
abstracts, searches, due-diligence files, acquisition memoranda,
legal/property correspondence, Land Registry correspondence, planning
records and communications with public authorities.

Please ensure that no routine retention, deletion, destruction, disposal or
overwriting process removes potentially relevant material. This
preservation request includes electronic files, archived mailboxes and
other electronically stored information where applicable.

The public evidence index and supporting record are maintained at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

Nothing in this correspondence abandons, limits or prejudices any claim
concerning title, registration, █████, deliberate concealment, procedural
unfairness, public-authority involvement, limitation, reopening of historic
proceedings, rectification/alteration of the register, compensation or
reparations. All rights and remedies are expressly reserved.

This correspondence is not a claim form and does not constitute service of
proceedings.

Please acknowledge receipt and refer this correspondence to Persimmon's
legal/property team. I request a substantive response addressing the
questions above.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

NEXT SUNDAY: ROAD CLOSURES
FOR CARDIFF HALF MARATHON


**
------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Requester

Road closures will affect our community on the morning of Sunday 4th October for the Cardiff Half Marathon.

Penarth Road, Barry Road and Cogan Spur will all be closed, as the marathon course runs along these roads.

Llandough Hill will also be closed, to prevent vehicles diverted via Penlan Road from inadvertently trying to access Penarth Road while it's shut.
Diversions will be in place, and you can see the full road closure map above.

The closures will operate between 9am and 12pm.

Further details can be found at the Cardiff Half Marathon website here.  (https://www.cardiffhalfmarathon.co.uk/event-info/road-closures/)

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1BzkRccTvm/

If you have further questions, Requester, please let me know.


**
------------------------------------------------------------

Next community litter pick

Our last community litter pick has had great feedback.

I've even had a couple of messages asking when the next one is taking place!

Llandough Community Council organise these events throughout the year, but they usually put them on hold during the winter, due to lack of interest.

But given the enthusiasm, I thought it best to harness it!

We discussed it at last week's Community Council meeting, and I'm exploring organising another in the coming weeks.

I'll need to liaise with the Vale Council to arrange equipment, but the Community Council are on board and have said they'll help.

If you're interested in taking part, Requester, drop me a message!
https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1KDWx1SUjX/

Licensing Service of
Revd Phil Maudsley

I had a wonderful evening on Tuesday at the Licensing Service of Reverend Phil Maudsley, the new Penarth Ministry Area lead.

It was great to see many members of our community there, including Llandough Community Council Chair Mo Misra, Reverend Susannah Griffin and lots of other residents.

Phil and his family have recently moved to South Wales from North Yorkshire, and I look forward to working with him.

I know everyone in Llandough will join me in welcoming them to our community.

Greenway Close verge

When I was out in our village recently, a Greenway Close resident raised the overgrowth on the nearby verge.

As you'll see from the first picture, it was in need of attention.

I raised with the Council. And I'm pleased to report it's now been cut back.

Thanks so much to the resident for coming over and raising this.

It helped ensure it was cleared.

As I always say, we're a team in Llandough.

By all chipping in, we make our village better for everyone.

If you ever spot anything that needs attention, Requester, do let me know!

Preventing car thefts

Sirs/ Ma'ams,

I need to correct a date I have used in earlier correspondence about Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, titles WA231076 and WA240304.

I had treated 1983 as the year the two titles were merged. That was wrong. HM Land Registry’s own letter of 23 March 2026 (Lisa Griffiths, ref N610CGV) separates the two acts.
1982–83 was first registration of two live titles, not a merger.
30 November 1982: application to first-register WA231076. The Court of Appeal later treated BP Properties Ltd as registered proprietors of “the farm” from November 1982.
23 February 1983: application to first-register a second title, WA240304.
26 March 1983: Mary Williams died. On the family’s case, notice of those applications did not reach us until after her death, while the family was in mourning. She had no window in which to object. The family was not in a position to use any window that arrived after that.
Those two titles remained separate through first instance.
24 July 1986: Hollis J. Both titles were still live. The judgment language treats Great House Farm as one holding. It had not been one holding on the register. On the family’s case it had not been one holding since the 1877 split: Parcel A (house, buildings, garden/yard and about 10 acres, the Thomas/Williams line) and Parcel B (the eastern fields retained by Bute and later WGR/BP).
2 February 1987: application to amalgamate the two titles. WA240304 was then closed and registration continued under WA231076. That is the merge. It was made after the 1986 ruling and before the Court of Appeal gave judgment on 31 July 1987.
So 1983 is silent first registration of a second title while Mary was still in Parcel A, or had only just died. 1987 is the administrative merger, carried out while the appeal was still open.
This was not a dispute about a single land parcel that BP already owned. Mary was on Parcel A, which the family █████ she owned, with occupation on that house parcel running in the family from at least 1667. BP, and WGR before it from 1949, were the neighbouring interest on Parcel B. From 1949 onwards the family’s case is that those neighbours ran a decades-long series of tenancy offers, “whole farm” wording, possession orders and the 1974 letters to make her occupation of her own parcel look permissive, and to make both parcels look like one estate they had acquired. They never produced a conveyance of Parcel A. What they had was an unfounded claim that her occupancy was permissive.
Please treat any earlier letter from me that said the titles merged in 1983 as corrected by this email. The dates that matter are:
1982/83 — first registration of two titles, without the occupier being heard;
24 July 1986 — first-instance judgment describing one farm while two titles still stood;
2 February 1987 — amalgamation, before the appeal ended;
31 July 1987 — Court of Appeal.
Yours faithfully,

Requester
Refs where relevant: N610CGV; 260919-6726246; titles WA231076 and WA240304.

> Dr Misra,
> 
> Thank you for replying, and for doing so promptly and at a weekend. 
> Good drills Sir. What an honour. I know you and the Council serve as 
> volunteers, and I am grateful for the time.

> Let me set out plainly what I am asking of the Council, which is 
> narrow. If you'll allow me?

> I am not asking your Council to revisit Mr Egan's answer of 14 June 
> 2026. He explained that the minute books from 1982 onwards were 
> deposited with Glamorgan Archives in 2002, and I am pursuing those

> Community Council is a public authority under Schedule 1, Part II, 
> paragraph 7(b) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000. The Act applies 
> to the recorded information set out below generally; the Environmental 
> Information Regulations 2004 apply in addition to any part of it that 
> is environmental information.

> 
> 1. Whether the Council holds any recorded information created after the 
> 2002 deposit -- minutes, correspondence, reports, emails, photographs 
> or files of any kind -- concerning Great House Farm (Ty Mawr) / Church 
> View Close, the village green in front of St Dochdwy's including 
> registered green VG 41, or the roadside verge by the churchyard wall.

> the farm, the barn, the green or the church surroundings, of any date.

> anything, transferred to it from Penarth Town Council at the 1982 
> reorganisation, and any recorded information identifying where the 
> pre-1982 Llandough community records were deposited.

> 16 October 2026.
>

> written refusal notice identifying the exemption or exception relied 
> on; section 17(7) requires the Council to give particulars of any 
> complaints procedure it operates, or to state that it has none, and to 
> notify me of my right to apply to the Information Commissioner; and 
> regulation 11 gives a right to an internal review of any refusal under 
> the EIR.
>

> complain to the Information Commissioner.

>

> simply things I would be grateful for.

> am asking whether the Council would be willing to pass my details to 
> any former member, former clerk or long-standing resident who might 
> remember the village between the 1950s and the 1990s, leaving it 
> entirely to them whether to contact me. I appreciate the Council may 
> have data protection or administrative reasons for declining, and I 
> would not press it.
> 
> B. Whether the Council would be willing to table this correspondence at 
> a meeting and minute it. I am content for it to be tabled in full.
> 
> C. Whether the Council would consider, in due course, whether an 
> interpretation board or a plaque near the green would be appropriate.

> burials, described in the published report as by far the largest early 
> medieval burial population so far recovered from Wales, above a Roman 
> villa and an Iron Age roundhouse. That history belongs to Llandough as 
> much as to my family, and there is nothing on the ground that records 
> it. I would be glad to give the Council or the community a short talk 
> on the documentary record, without charge, if that would be useful.
> 
> I should be grateful for a response to items 1 to 3 by 16 October 2026.
> 
> Regards,
>

records.transcript:
Dear Ms Applegate,

Thank you for your letter of 28 September 2026 acknowledging my emails of
26 and 27 September, and for allocating reference ICR/090/26. I note that
an investigation officer will contact me within ten working days.

I would like to place four further points on the file for the investigation
officer, in addition to those already set out in my emails.

1. Public record

Please treat https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ as part of the
material already cited.

The landing page sets out, diagrammatically and with links to the
underlying evidence, the family’s case that Parcel A — the farmhouse,
garden and associated land on the Williams/Thomas line — was included
within a whole-farm registered title even though the documentary root by
which BP acquired that parcel remains unresolved.

Our paper title deed being █████ from our home resulting in us not able to
be present in court in 1974 (and so ownership adjudication was ajourned and
our ownership assertion was weakened (not exstiguished) we understand. But
the stretch of the imagine it takes to ever believe it was Western Ground
Rents or BPs is all based on absurdity after absurdity and does not in my
estimation, meet the criteria of what a sane, reasonable person would do.

The website greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
deliberately distinguishes documentary records from family evidence,
reconstruction and unresolved inference. I am therefore not asking ICR to
accept every proposition on the site as established fact; I am asking that
the underlying records and the specific questions identified there be
considered.

2. Chronology now recorded by HM Land Registry

I had earlier written as if the two titles merged in 1983. That was wrong.
HM Land Registry’s letter of 23 March 2026 (Lisa Griffiths, ref N610CGV)
separates the first-registration events from the later amalgamation. My
correction of 27 September is already on your file.

The chronology that now matters is:

• 30 November 1982 — application to first-register WA231076.

• 23 February 1983 — application to first-register WA240304.

• 26 March 1983 — Mary Williams died. Our family’s account is that notice
of BP’s registration was received only after her death, during/ after that
mourning period. Whether that account can be established from the notice,
service and correspondence records is itself a question for investigation.

• 24 July 1986 — Hollis J. The historical title material still showed both
titles live.

• 2 February 1987 — an application to amalgamate the two titles was
recorded. WA240304 was subsequently closed and registration continued under
WA231076. This is the amalgamation event, distinct from the 1982/83 first
registrations. It occurred while the BP Properties Ltd v Buckler litigation
was still live and before the Court of Appeal judgment of 31 July 1987.

• *14 April 1989 — Buckler v United Kingdom was declared inadmissible by
the European Commission of Human Rights.*

I regard this as a further institutional failure that now requires
reconsideration. The decision treated BP as having rights in our land
parcel and referred to BP as the owners, although BP had been awarded
possession, not ownership, and ownership of Parcel A had never been
adjudicated in BP’s favour. The distinction is fundamental. Possession is
not the same thing as ownership, and an order for possession did not itself
determine that BP had acquired the underlying proprietary interest in
Parcel A.

On the family’s case, our ownership claim to Parcel A was never
extinguished. The question therefore is not simply whether BP obtained
possession through the proceedings, but whether any legal process ever
transferred, extinguished or superseded the family’s underlying proprietary
interest. If it did not, the basis upon which BP was subsequently treated
as having superior rights in the parcel requires examination.

That issue also goes directly to the later assertion that the family’s
occupation became “permissive” under BP’s 1974 licence letters. A party
cannot ordinarily confer a proprietary right it does not itself possess. If
BP did not own Parcel A, it is necessary to establish what legal interest
BP actually held that enabled it to grant my grandmother, or anyone else,
permissive occupation of that parcel — particularly where there had already
been a long succession of earlier attempts to establish a permissive basis
for the family’s occupation.
The point is especially significant because the person whose occupation was
supposedly made permissive was herself the long-standing occupier and, on
the family’s case, the superior title holder of the parcel, with the
family’s occupation extending back centuries. I therefore ask that the
investigation distinguish carefully between *possession awarded to BP,
ownership of Parcel A, and any █████ power to license the family’s
occupation*. Those are not interchangeable propositions, and the
documentary basis for treating them as such requires examination.

3. What I am asking ICR to review

HM Land Registry has told my MP, and said in its stage-two decision of 25
May 2026, that the title was registered correctly and that there is no
evidence of a mistake. That is the institutional position my family has
encountered for decades.

I am not asking ICR to determine title. I am asking whether that conclusion
was reached after a proper examination of the first-registration files and,
in particular:

• the documentary basis and extent claimed for Parcel A in the
first-registration applications;

• the missing 31 December 1969 conveyance and the 1971 abstract of title;

• the notice and service records, including what notice was given to the
occupier, when, and what effective opportunity existed to object;

• the three inconsistent closure dates now appearing in the HMLR record for
WA240304; and

• the 2 February 1987 amalgamation application, including what was actually
amalgamated, on what plans and documents, and what title information
existed at that point in the still-live litigation.

The concern is therefore not simply one of hindsight. Much of the relevant
material was created contemporaneously with the events in question. That is
why I raise mistake, concealment and procedural unfairness as matters
requiring investigation, rather than as findings I am asking you to make at
this acknowledgement stage.

4. Why the record was reconstructed from Y Wladfa

For almost two years I have been in the Welsh Settlement in Patagonia,
rebuilding a replica of the farmhouse in which I was born.

That reconstruction prompted me to revisit the documentary history of Great
House Farm and, in doing so, to compare the family evidence with the
surviving land-registration, court and archival records. That work is what
brought the title chronology and the unresolved Parcel A question back into
focus.

The replica is also a way of preserving the history of a house that was
demolished in December 1988. I mention this not as an argument on the
merits, but to explain why a historical record that had remained largely
unexamined for decades was reconstructed now, and why I have pursued the
underlying documents rather than relying solely on inherited family
accounts.

Y Wladfa itself exists because Michael D. Jones and those who followed him
judged that Welsh language, history, heritage, people, landscape and
buildings were being overwritten in Wales — the process they cited as the
work of a “decapitation committee”. Which makes it interesting 99% of UK
MPs refused to sign an EDM in 2025 condemning us Christians being
decapitated. Our land parcel was clearly a Christian stronghold and holy
sacred lands and we were clearly stewards of it for centuries.

The Patagonia Welsh settlement is where those things are instead kept,
celebrated and respected. The replica stands there for the same reason the
original house cannot stand on Parcel A.

I will wait to hear from the investigation officer.

I also take this opportunity to draw your attention to the enclosed PDF,
which contains photographs relating to a tree-planting ceremony on the
southernmost part of our claimed Parcel A and subsequent photographs
showing the tree being demolished. The ceremony is part of the family’s
evidence of its assertion of ownership: my great-grandfather is recorded as
planting the tree to commemorate that ownership. The photographs also
preserve contemporaneous visual evidence, including identifiable
individuals and machinery vehicle registration numbers, which may assist in
establishing who carried out the later destruction and in what
circumstances.

There is a further land-history issue which may be relevant to the wider
question of how our claimed parcel came to be treated as no longer
belonging to the family. The woodland to the north of our home, on our
claimed parcel, was taken at a time when my grandmother had undergone a leg
amputation in 1955 and had become wheelchair-bound. I understand that this
woodland was subsequently gifted to a charity, which has itself contacted
me recently; I enclose that correspondence with the present material.

Similarly, I understand that land to the south of the farmhouse was also
taken, notwithstanding that the 1955 possession order appears, on the
documentary material presently available to me, to have concerned the
parcel to the east of ours. The Council subsequently made the southern land
into a small green or park and, in the process, the commemorative tree and
other physical evidence of the family’s assertion of ownership were
destroyed. I appreciate that this moves beyond the immediate registration
question, but the destruction of physical evidence bearing directly upon
the family's historic claim may be relevant to understanding the subsequent
evidential position.

There is also a further matter which I mention cautiously because I do not
yet know its full significance. It has been █████ to me that the
long-serving Council Clerk for Llandough played a role in the destruction
of this evidence. When I initially raised the matter through FOI, his
response was, as I understand it, an attempt not to become involved. When
subsequently required to respond, he retired after approximately 35 years'
service. I am not asserting that these events establish misconduct or that
his retirement was connected with this matter; I do not presently know the
extent, if any, of the connection.

I include the material because I believe it may have evidential relevance,
whether to the immediate investigation or, if not, at a later stage when
the wider history of the land and the disappearance of evidence is
considered. The tree ceremony, its subsequent destruction, the photographs,
and the associated correspondence provide material evidence which I do not
think should be disregarded simply because some aspects of it may
ultimately fall outside the immediate scope of this review.

There is also an important cultural dimension to the evidence. The tree was
not merely a physical object: its planting appears to have been an act of
asserting and commemorating ownership █████ the family’s
longstanding traditions and understanding of the land. I recognise that
questions of ancient custom and tradition may not fall within the immediate
legal scope of ICR/090/26. I mention them because the destruction of the
physical manifestation of that assertion removed evidence of the very claim
whose documentary survival is now being investigated.

Regards,

Requester

*FORMAL PRESERVATION NOTICE*
*Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth*
*Titles: WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527*
*Planning references: 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES*

*URL: **greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com
 *

*To each recipient separately, in your own capacity as a current or
potential holder, custodian or controller of relevant records:*

This notice is addressed to each recipient *individually*. It is *not a
joint request*, and it does not ask any recipient to speak for, investigate
on behalf of, or answer in place of any other person or organisation. Each
recipient is asked to respond only in respect of records within that
recipient's own possession, custody or control, including records inherited
from a predecessor organisation or retained on its behalf.
1. Nature and purpose of this notice

This is a *formal preservation notice* concerning documentary material
relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, adjoining
St Dochdwy's, and the subsequent development of the site, including the
area now associated with Church View Close.

It is *not a claim form, is not service of proceedings, and is not intended
to constitute or replace any FOI request, internal review, complaint,
subject-access request or other statutory process already made to any
recipient.*

The purpose of this notice is to require the preservation of potentially
relevant material while the documentary history, title chain, registration
history, planning history, possession proceedings, demolition and
subsequent development are being reconstructed.

A separate first-stage preservation notice has been issued or is being
issued to Cadw / Welsh Government FOI, HM Land Registry Wales Office and
DPO, Heneb / GGAT HER, RCAHMW, Vale of Glamorgan FOI Unit and DPO,
Glamorgan Archives, South Wales Police FOI, The National Archives, the
Wales Office FOI team, and the National Library of Wales. Persimmon Homes
(Wales) Ltd has received a separate preservation letter.

*You are receiving this notice separately because the published documentary
record places you, or a predecessor whose records may remain in your
custody or control, within the documentary, legal, professional,
administrative or development chain concerning this land.*
2. Land and documentary scope

Please preserve, and do not destroy, alter, overwrite, discard, transfer
out of custody without a recorded handover, or otherwise dispose of, any
record within your possession, custody or control relating to the land or
matters identified below.

The scope includes, without limitation, *originals, copies, working papers,
drafts, annotations, plans, photographs, negatives, films, tapes, maps,
registers, indexes, correspondence, emails and attachments, electronic
files, archived mailboxes, databases, metadata, internal notes, meeting
records, instructions, client or matter files, survey material and other
associated records.*

The material requested includes:

*1. Historical ownership, occupation and conveyancing*

The 1877 split; the 1916 and 1939 tenancies; the 1938 Bute to Western
Ground Rents conveyance; the 1969 Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust
conveyance; and any plans, schedules, abstracts, searches, correspondence
or other documents relied upon in relation to those transactions.

*2. Possession proceedings and subsequent litigation*

The █████ and █████ possession orders; the
1974 proceedings; *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2*; House of
Lords leave papers, including *YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536*; and *Buckler v United
Kingdom (1989)*, including associated correspondence, instructions,
evidence, plans and working papers.

*3. Land registration*

The first registration of *WA231076*, including the application dated 30
November 1982; the first registration of *WA240304*, including the
application dated 23 February 1983; subsequent amalgamation, transfer or
closure; and every plan, conveyance, abstract, search, application,
correspondence trail or professional file relied upon in connection with
those registrations or changes.

*4. 1988 possession and demolition*

The taking of possession on or about *29 November 1988* and the demolition
commenced on or about *6 December 1988*, including any planning,
listed-building, heritage, police, enforcement, media, contractor, survey,
photographic or inter-agency liaison material.

*5. Planning and subsequent development, 1989–1996*

Planning application *89/01396/OUT*; reserved matters application
*92/00671/RES*; conditions 16–18; GGAT / Cotswold Archaeology material;
records concerning any *section 52, section 106, planning obligation, local
land charge or equivalent instrument*; and the transfer from BP to Ideal
Homes dated *3 December 1993*, together with all associated plans,
correspondence, approvals, agreements, searches and completion material.

*6. Family records*

Records concerning *Mary Doreen Williams (died 1983)* and *William Buckler*,
insofar as those records relate to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, the land
described above, its occupation, ownership, possession, disposal,
registration, development or demolition.
3. Predecessor and inherited files

Where you hold, or may hold, a file originating with a predecessor,
successor, merged practice, affiliated practice, client or other entity,
that material is also within scope.

This includes, without limitation, records originating from:

*Loosemores of Cardiff; Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn / Blake Morgan;
Linklaters & Paines; Debenham Tewson / DTZ / Cushman & Wakefield; Wyn
Thomas + Partners; Ideal Homes Wales; BP Properties; BP Pension Trust;
Cotswold Archaeological Trust; Cardiff Bay Development Corporation; and
South Glamorgan County Council.*

The reference to a predecessor file does not assert that you necessarily
hold such a file. It identifies material for which a reasonable custody or
succession inquiry should be made where applicable.
4. Preservation steps

Please take reasonable steps to prevent the routine destruction, deletion,
alteration or overwriting of potentially relevant material, including
material held in *archived mailboxes, legacy systems, off-site storage,
document-management systems, backup repositories and other electronic or
physical stores*.

Where relevant material has been transferred to another repository,
archive, successor organisation or third party, please preserve the
information necessary to identify the transfer and its current location,
including any accession, file, box, reference or custody details.

Nothing in this notice requires the creation of records that do not exist.
The request concerns the preservation of records already held or controlled
by you.
5. Purpose and legal position

This notice is *not a finding against any recipient*, and I am not asking
any recipient to determine title or adjudicate the underlying dispute.

The *1987 Court of Appeal judgment* is relied upon here only for matters
actually determined by that judgment, including the issues concerning
possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. This preservation
notice does not treat that judgment as having determined the complete
documentary root of title to the farmhouse parcel.

The underlying documentary history, including the relationship between the
farmhouse parcel and the agricultural land subsequently dealt with through
Western Ground Rents and BP, remains a matter requiring reconstruction from
the primary records.

Accordingly, preservation is requested precisely so that the documentary
record can be established from the records themselves rather than through
assumptions based on later registration, later occupation, later planning
treatment or secondary descriptions.
6. Acknowledgement and identification of records

Please acknowledge receipt of this notice and, in your own capacity,
confirm:

*(a)* the officer, partner, records manager or other person responsible for
implementing the preservation hold;

*(b)* what records within your possession, custody or control you have
identified as falling within the scope above; and

*(c)* where you identify no records within scope, what relevant systems,
files, repositories or predecessor records you searched in reaching that
conclusion.

A substantive assessment of title is not requested from you. The immediate
requirement is preservation and identification of the documentary material
you hold.

The public documentary index and developing evidence record is available at:

*https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
 *

Please monitor that site for subsequent identification of documents,
references and specific schedules relevant to your organisation's records.

Where a reliable public email address is unavailable, a postal preservation
notice will also be sent. For example, a postal notice will follow to
*Loosemores,
Alliance House, 18–█████, Cardiff █████*.

Nothing in this notice constitutes an abandonment, waiver or limitation of
any claim, position or remedy concerning *title, registration, concealment,
limitation, reopening, rectification or alteration of the register, or any
associated matter.*

Regards,

*Requester *
**
